To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The application of disinfectants is the most effective and successful intervention to reduce waterborne disease.

(a) new pathogens are emerging, (b) WSPs are crucial to maintaining public health, (c) chlorine based disinfectants remain the most common disinfectants used in the water treatment industry, and (d) new disinfection technologies, including those based on nanotechnology, are needed to ensure that waterborne pathogens are inactivated adequately and that DBP formation is minimized.
1) Waterborne diseases are still a serious public health problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the best disinfection strategies to achieve the highest levels of water quality and safety, while minimizing the formation of DBPs.

the development of novel and/or improved disinfection strategies that will provide a high level of protection against waterborne microbial diseases while maintaining a low risk for the formation of DBPs.

the identification, characterization and inactivation of microbial pathogens in water, the development and application of new disinfection technologies, and the assessment of the risks of exposure to microbial pathogens and DBPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single disinfectant that is best for all water quality situations.

the current state of the art in drinking water disinfectants is that the best approach is to use a combination of different disinfectant processes, and to use them in an optimized manner, to ensure the highest level of disinfection and the lowest level of disinfection by products.

, while there is a need to continue to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of disinfectants in drinking water treatment, the most important factor in maintaining the health of the public is the application of a comprehensive WSP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of new and improved disinfection technologies, and the use of existing disinfectants in novel ways, will be crucial to the future of drinking water disinfection.
, although there has been considerable progress in the field of drinking water disinfection, there are still many areas that need further research.
there are many new and innovative technologies that have been developed to address the challenges of disinfecting drinking water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
water disinfection is a critical step in protecting public health.
water treatment technologies should be evaluated based on their ability to achieve health targets.
the use of nanotechnology in drinking water disinfections may offer new and effective solutions for waterborne pathogens.
